name: Israel at the first Passover
charge: Doing as the Lord commanded Moses and Aaron: the lamb, the blood on the door, the unleavened bread
summary: On the night the destroyer went through Egypt, every house of Israel that did as it was told was passed over. The children of Israel went away, and did as the Lord had commanded Moses and Aaron, so did they. The ordinance was made perpetual on the spot.
offense: Take you a lamb according to the house of your fathers; kill it in the evening; take of the blood and strike it on the two side posts and on the upper door post; eat it with unleavened bread and bitter herbs, in haste; none of you shall go out at the door of his house until the morning. And the children of Israel went away, and did as the Lord had commanded Moses and Aaron, so did they. By faith he kept the passover, and the sprinkling of blood, lest he that destroyed the firstborn should touch them.
judgment: The blood shall be to you for a token upon the houses where ye are: and when I see the blood, I will pass over you, and the plague shall not be upon you to destroy you. At midnight the Lord smote all the firstborn in the land of Egypt, and against the children of Israel not so much as a dog moved his tongue. He brought them forth also with silver and gold: and there was not one feeble person among their tribes. Thus did all the children of Israel; as the Lord commanded Moses and Aaron, so did they. And it came to pass the selfsame day.

entries.commentary: This month shall be unto you the beginning of months, the first month of the year. The month is Abib, the month in which Israel came out of Egypt. Abib in the Bible dictionary is the pre-exilic name for the first month of the year; after the exile the name was changed to Nisan, and it falls between March and April. So the new year begins in the springtime, around March and April, not on January the first in the dead of winter; that is another lie taught in Babylon.

In the tenth day of the month every man was to take a lamb according to the house of his fathers; if the household was too little for the lamb, he and his neighbour next unto his house were to take it according to the number of the souls. The lamb was to be without blemish, a male of the first year, taken from the sheep or from the goats. This is a foreshadowing: the feast days and sacrifices are a shadow of things to come, but the body is of Christ. The lamb without blemish and without spot points to Christ, who was sinless, verily foreordained before the foundation of the world but manifest in these last times for the nation of Israel.

The whole assembly of the congregation of Israel was to kill the lamb in the evening, and take of the blood and strike it on the two side posts and on the upper door post of the houses. The flesh was to be eaten that night, roast with fire, with unleavened bread and with bitter herbs. That is the Passover menu in layman's terms: lamb roast with fire, unleavened bread, bitter herbs; no fried chicken, no birthday cake, no mashed potatoes and gravy, none of the thirteen herbs and spices.

Eat not of it raw, nor sodden at all with water: do not boil it, but roast it with fire, the head with the legs and the purtenance thereof, and let nothing of it remain until the morning; what remains is burned with fire. It was to be eaten with loins girded, shoes on the feet, and staff in hand, in haste: it is the Lord's passover, and that very night Israel was leaving Egypt.

The Lord would pass through the land that night and smite all the firstborn of man and beast, and against all the gods of Egypt he would execute judgment. Each plague put an Egyptian god to shame: when he smote the land with darkness he showed that the sun god Ra is no god at all, for the God of heaven and earth blotted out the sun three days. Israel had to learn that those gods are nothing, because the nation was about to come out and serve the one true God. The blood was a token upon the houses: when I see the blood, I will pass over you. That is where the term Passover comes from; the houses with the blood on the doorposts were passed over from death while the firstborn of Egypt were slain.

This day is a memorial, a feast to the Lord throughout your generations, kept by an ordinance for ever. It was not done away; even in the New Testament the Passover is still kept: Christ our passover is sacrificed for us, therefore let us keep the feast. The lamb of the Passover represents Christ, and the apostle's instruction is to keep the feast, not to spiritualize it away.

Seven days shall ye eat unleavened bread; even the first day the leaven is put out of the houses, and whosoever eats leavened bread from the first day until the seventh, that soul shall be cut off from Israel. The first day and the seventh day are holy convocations; no manner of work is done in them save that which every man must eat, meaning the food may be cooked. The feast of unleavened bread is observed because in this selfsame day the Most High brought the armies of Israel out of Egypt. He deals with armies, and when he brings Israel out of this place he is bringing out an army again: when the spirit of life enters them and they stand upon their feet, great fear falls on them which see them, for they stand up an exceeding great army, not choir boys.

In the first month, on the fourteenth day of the month at even, ye shall eat unleavened bread, until the one and twentieth day of the month at even. The Passover begins and ends at even because the day begins and ends at even; it is not difficult. Sin puts blinders on: when you hate your brother you are in darkness and cannot see what the scripture plainly says. Many fell away from the truth over this very point of the day beginning at evening. For seven days no leaven is found in the houses; whoever eats that which is leavened, whether stranger or born in the land, is cut off from the congregation of Israel.

The elders were to draw out a lamb for their families and kill the passover, take a bunch of hyssop, dip it in the blood in the bason, and strike the lintel and the two side posts; the hyssop bush was used like a paintbrush to paint the blood of the lamb over the doorposts. None of you shall go out at the door of his house until the morning: stay inside, for the Lord passes through to smite the Egyptians, and where he sees the blood he will pass over the door and will not suffer the destroyer to come in to smite you. The destroyer was Christ, the almighty word of God. In the quiet silence of that night the almighty word leaped down from heaven out of the royal throne as a fierce man of war into the midst of the land of destruction, and standing up filled all things with death. The Egyptians cried for the children that were bewailed; master and servant, king and common person suffered after one manner, and the dead were too many to bury. Upon the destruction of the firstborn they acknowledged this people to be the sons of God.

This thing is an ordinance to thee and to thy sons for ever, kept even when Israel comes into the land the Lord promised. When the children ask, What mean ye by this service? the answer is, It is the sacrifice of the Lord's passover, who passed over the houses of the children of Israel in Egypt when he smote the Egyptians and delivered our houses. The feast days commemorate the Most High delivering his people and bringing judgment on their enemies; that is the same pattern the feast of dedication commemorates. The people bowed the head and worshipped, and the children of Israel went and did as the Lord had commanded Moses and Aaron.

At midnight the Lord smote all the firstborn in the land of Egypt, from the firstborn of Pharaoh that sat on his throne unto the firstborn of the captive in the dungeon, and all the firstborn of cattle. Even the prisoners' firstborn died, and Pharaoh's own son died. In this Christ showed that Osiris and Isis, the supposed Egyptian gods of life and death, control neither life nor death. Unto God the Lord belong the issues from death; the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob is the God of salvation, and he alone brings forth death.

Pharaoh rose up in the night, he and all his servants and all the Egyptians, and there was a great cry in Egypt, for there was not a house where there was not one dead. The last time Pharaoh saw Moses he threatened to kill him if he ever saw his face again; now he called for Moses and Aaron by night, saying, Rise up, get you forth from among my people, go, serve the Lord as ye have said, take your flocks and your herds, and bless me also. Touch not mine anointed, and do my prophets no harm; the man who thought he could threaten the servant of the Most High had a complete change of tone. The Egyptians were urgent upon the people to send them out of the land in haste, for they said, We be all dead men.

The people took their dough before it was leavened, their kneadingtroughs bound up in their clothes upon their shoulders. As Moses had said, they borrowed of the Egyptians jewels of silver, and jewels of gold, and raiment; the Lord gave the people favour in the sight of the Egyptians, so that they lent them what they required, and they spoiled the Egyptians. They took everything.

The children of Israel journeyed from Rameses to Succoth, about six hundred thousand on foot that were men, beside children. Israel departed from Rameses in the first month; the exodus is tied to Rameses by name.

A mixed multitude went up also with them, and flocks and herds, even very much cattle. The mixed multitude that left with Israel were not to be among the children of Israel as rulers. The law sets the order: bondmen and bondmaids are to be of the heathen round about and of the strangers that sojourn among you; they are a possession and an inheritance for the children. But over the brethren, the children of Israel, ye shall not rule one over another with rigour.

They baked unleavened cakes of the dough brought out of Egypt, for it was not leavened, because they were thrust out of Egypt and could not tarry, neither had they prepared any victual. The sojourning of the children of Israel who dwelt in Egypt was four hundred and thirty years, and at the end of the four hundred and thirty years, even the selfsame day, all the hosts of the Lord went out from the land of Egypt. It is a night to be much observed unto the Lord for bringing them out from the land of Egypt: this is the Passover night, which all the children of Israel are to observe in their generations.

This is the ordinance of the passover: no stranger eats of it. A bought servant may eat when he is circumcised; a foreigner and an hired servant shall not eat thereof. When a stranger will keep the passover of the Lord, let all his males be circumcised, and he shall be as one born in the land; one law is to the homeborn and to the stranger. It is eaten in one house, none of the flesh carried outside, neither shall ye break a bone thereof. That also goes to Christ, the Passover lamb, whose bones were not broken on the cross. Thus did all the children of Israel as the Lord commanded Moses and Aaron, and the selfsame day the Lord brought them out of the land of Egypt by their armies.

The Most High already knew what was going down: yet will I bring one plague more upon Pharaoh and upon Egypt. This last plague would end it, and when Pharaoh let the people go he would thrust them out hence altogether, with the quickness.

Every man and woman was to borrow of their neighbours jewels of silver and jewels of gold, and the Lord gave the people favour in the sight of the Egyptians. Moses was very great in the land of Egypt, in the sight of Pharaoh's servants and in the sight of the people; he had a good report. Israel in spiritual Egypt must deal the same way: have the respect of the people, and if people despise you, let it be because they hate God and the word you teach, not because you are in wickedness, shady dealings, deceit, or disrespect.

About midnight the Lord would go out into the midst of Egypt, and all the firstborn in the land would die, from the firstborn of Pharaoh on his throne to the firstborn of the maidservant behind the mill, and all the firstborn of beasts. There would be a great cry throughout all the land of Egypt, such as there was none like it, nor shall be like it any more.

Against the children of Israel not a dog would move his tongue, that ye may know how that the Lord doth put a difference between the Egyptians and Israel. A difference had to be shown because Israel and the Egyptians looked alike. Moses was mistaken for an Egyptian, Paul was mistaken for an Egyptian, Joseph was mistaken for an Egyptian by his own brothers, and at Jacob's funeral the mourners were called Egyptians because no one could tell the difference. The difference was made plain in the plague itself: the houses whose firstborn died were shown not to be his people.

All Pharaoh's servants would come down and bow to Moses, saying, Get thee out, and all the people that follow thee; and Moses went out from Pharaoh in a great anger. Pharaoh would not hearken, that the wonders of the Most High might be multiplied in the land of Egypt. He is in control of the leaders of every country, presidents, governors, senators, congressmen, and mayors alike; whoever gets in the seat, he twists and turns them about like the river.

Give thanks unto the Most High, call upon His name, and make known His deeds among the people. Sing unto Him, glory in His holy name, and let the heart of them that seek Him rejoice; seek His face forevermore. Remember His marvelous works, His wonders, and the judgments of His mouth. The Bible tells us to remember our past. -

O seed of Abraham and children of Jacob His chosen: the Most High is our God and His judgments are in all the earth. He has remembered His covenant forever, the word commanded to a thousand generations, made with Abraham, sworn to Isaac, confirmed to Jacob for a law and to Israel for an everlasting covenant. If Israel was to have an everlasting covenant, then the new covenant cannot suddenly involve all people. You must ask these questions of anyone who does not use the scriptures.

When they were few and strangers in the land, He suffered no man to wrong them and reproved kings for their sake: touch not mine anointed. He called a famine and sent a man before them, even Joseph, sold for a servant and bound with fetters until his word came to pass. The king loosed him and made him lord of his house and ruler of his substance, to bind his princes and teach his senators wisdom. Our forefather Joseph taught the Egyptians; those who boast in Egyptology forget our forefathers taught them. -

Israel came into Egypt and Jacob sojourned in the land of Ham; He increased His people and made them stronger than their enemies, then turned the Egyptians' hearts to hate them. He sent Moses and Aaron who showed His signs and wonders in the land of Ham; He recounts the plagues of darkness, blood, frogs, flies, lice, hail, fire, and locusts. The locusts and caterpillars devoured all the herbs and fruit of the ground; this is the devourer, and the Most High promises to rebuke the devourer for the sake of a righteous nation. He smote all the firstborn, the chief of all their strength. The firstborn is the chief of one's strength, as Reuben was Jacob's strength before he lost it. -

He brought Israel out with silver and gold, and there was not one feeble person among the tribes; look at the sicknesses we suffer now under the curses. He spread a cloud for a covering and fire for light, brought quails and the bread of heaven, and opened the rock so the waters gushed out in the dry place. He gave them the lands of the heathen and the labor of the people, that they might keep His statutes and laws. But we were not thankful, we went into idolatry, and now we are scattered in Babylon in America. -
